---
title: "Migrating to 1.0"
subtitle: "From 0.x, and from a site with its own theme"
toc: true
---

1.0 keeps the look of 0.5.1: the same colors, classes and CSS variables, so pages do not change appearance. What changes is configuration and a few things that were removed. This page lists both, then shows a step-by-step path.

## What changed

**The extension folder moved (breaking).** Quarto installs an extension from GitHub under the owner's folder, so a fresh `quarto add WFRCAnalytics/wfrc-brand` or `quarto use template` puts it at `_extensions/WFRCAnalytics/wfrc-brand/`. Earlier setups and the README used `_extensions/wfrc-brand/`. Every path in 1.0 includes the owner folder. A path that points at a folder that does not exist is **ignored without an error**: the site renders, unthemed.

**Added**

- `format: wfrc-brand-revealjs` for slides and a fuller `wfrc-brand-typst` for PDF reports, both from the same `brand.yml`.
- `brand-offline.yml`: the same brand with bundled font files (Poppins, Inter, Fira Code; OFL), for offline builds. `brand.yml` still loads fonts from Google Fonts.
- `brand-flat.yml`, the brand with light values only, for Shiny, R and Python (their brand.yml packages do not read light/dark pairs).
- Starter template: `quarto use template WFRCAnalytics/wfrc-brand`.
- Components promoted from the wfrcanalytics.github.io site: status chips (`.chip-live`, `.chip-internal`, `.chip-archived`), `.wfrc-stat-num`, rounded table listings, `.wfrc-cite` and `.wfrc-shot`.
- A fix for the repo-actions (GitHub) navbar dropdown running off the screen.

**Removed (breaking)**

| Removed | Use instead |
|---|---|
| Palette aliases `wfrc-blue`, `wfrc-secondary-blue`, `wfrc-yellow` (and `$brand-wfrc-blue` etc.) | `wfrc-navy`, `wfrc-bright-blue`, `wfrc-gold` |
| Legacy classes `#bio`, `#landing-icons`, `.name-highlight`, `.featured-image`, `.description a` | `.wfrc-*` components, or your own CSS |
| `engine: knitr`, `knitr.opts_chunk.dev: ragg_png` and `jupyter: python3` from `wfrc-shared.yml` | Quarto picks the engine from your code cells. Set `engine:` or `dev:` in your own `_quarto.yml` if you need them. |

**Changed in 1.0.1**

| Before | Now |
|---|---|
| The GitHub navbar menu linked every site to the wfrcanalytics.github.io repository | It points at **each site's own repository automatically** (from `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` or the git remote), so delete any GitHub menu of your own: `navbar.tools` GitHub block, or `repo-url` with `repo-actions`. "Ask a Question" shows only when the repository has Discussions on. |
| Contact and Terms of use in the footer were site-relative, so every site needed its own `contact/index.qmd` and `terms/index.qmd` | They link to the single pages on wfrcanalytics.github.io. Sites carry no copy; the `templates/` folder is gone. |
| `page-navigation: false` and `back-to-top-navigation: false` were set in the shared file, so a site could not turn them on | Not set (they are Quarto's defaults). Set them in your own `_quarto.yml`. |
| No way to differ from the shared defaults, because a value in the shared file beats your `_quarto.yml` | Put your differences in a `_site.yml` listed after the shared file; it beats the shared file. |

Class names, `--wfrc-*` and `--brand-*` variables and the page structure are unchanged.

## From 0.x

1. Replace the extension: delete `_extensions/wfrc-brand/` if you have it, then run `quarto add WFRCAnalytics/wfrc-brand`. It installs to `_extensions/WFRCAnalytics/wfrc-brand/`.
2. In `_quarto.yml` and any SCSS, CSS, `.qmd` or script that names the old folder, change `_extensions/wfrc-brand/` to `_extensions/WFRCAnalytics/wfrc-brand/`: `project.brand`, `metadata-files`, `project.resources`, listing `image:` paths and chart-helper imports. Then search your SCSS, CSS and `.qmd` files for the removed names above and replace them.
3. If your site relied on the R or Python engine defaults, add them to your `_quarto.yml`:

   ```yaml
   engine: knitr
   knitr:
     opts_chunk:
       dev: ragg_png
   ```

4. Render, clear `.quarto/` if styles look stale, and check a few pages in light and dark mode.
5. Delete CSS your site copied from the old extension. The status chips, table listings and card surface now come from the extension.

## From a site with its own theme

1. `quarto add WFRCAnalytics/wfrc-brand`, or start fresh with `quarto use template WFRCAnalytics/wfrc-brand` and move your content in.
2. Delete your own `_brand.yml`, theme SCSS, `format.html.theme`, `css:` and font links.
3. Add the two lines that connect the extension in `_quarto.yml`:

   ```yaml
   project:
     brand: _extensions/WFRCAnalytics/wfrc-brand/brand.yml
   metadata-files:
     - _extensions/WFRCAnalytics/wfrc-brand/wfrc-shared.yml
   ```

4. Remove anything `wfrc-shared.yml` already supplies. Quarto lists *append* across config levels, so a site that repeats the "Follow Us" menu or the footer links shows them twice.
5. Keep what is yours: `website.title`, `site-url`, `navbar.left`, sidebars, announcements and per-site GitHub links.
6. Do not add a GitHub menu: it points at your repository by itself. The footer's Contact and Terms of use links need nothing either: they go to the org pages.
7. Add the card banners to `project.resources` if you use grid listings:

   ```yaml
   project:
     resources:
       - _extensions/WFRCAnalytics/wfrc-brand/assets/cards/*.svg
   ```

## Overriding the shared defaults

A value in `wfrc-shared.yml` **beats the same key in your own `_quarto.yml`** (verified on Quarto 1.11), so editing your own file never changes an org default. Use a second metadata file listed after the shared one, which beats it:

```yaml
# _quarto.yml
metadata-files:
  - _extensions/WFRCAnalytics/wfrc-brand/wfrc-shared.yml
  - _site.yml
```

```yaml
# _site.yml: only what this site does differently
execute:
  freeze: false
format:
  html:
    toc-expand: 1
    grid:
      sidebar-width: 406px
website:
  back-to-top-navigation: true
```

Any key can be overridden this way, including `website.*`. Lists (navbar items, footer links) still **append** instead of replacing, so a site cannot remove the "Follow Us" menu, the GitHub menu or the footer links; it can only add to them.

Do not set `format: wfrc-brand-html` in a website that loads `wfrc-shared.yml`. The shared file defines `format.html`, so Quarto would render every page twice (as `html` and as `wfrc-brand-html`) and fail on the second write. Keep `wfrc-brand-html` for standalone documents.

## Good to know

- **Why `project.brand` is still needed.** Quarto does not discover a brand file inside an extension, and declaring `contributes.brand` does not change that (tested on Quarto 1.11). Without the path, the theme fails with `Undefined variable $brand-wfrc-paper`.
- **Why dashboards, slides and PDFs use their own format names.** Quarto applies an extension's format settings only to formats named after the extension: `wfrc-brand-dashboard`, `wfrc-brand-revealjs`, `wfrc-brand-typst`. Org defaults for plain `html` live in `wfrc-shared.yml` for that reason.
- **Slides and bundled fonts.** Quarto 1.11 does not copy bundled font files for revealjs, so slides use `brand.yml` (Google Fonts) even if the site uses `brand-offline.yml`.
- **Scripts.** Add your own scripts with `include-in-header` or `include-before-body`, not `include-after-body`: Quarto does not merge two `include-after-body` values, and the extension's accessibility script uses it.

See the [changelog](https://github.com/WFRCAnalytics/wfrc-brand/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) for every release.
